BiblicalUsage: The enchanter is the wise man of Babylon, the one the king calls when no one else can answer. The Chaldeans say there is no man on earth who can shew the king's matter, for no king has asked such things of any magician or astrologer or Chaldean; Daniel says the secret the king demands cannot be shewed by the wise men, the astrologers, the magicians or the soothsayers; and the queen remembers that in Daniel's father there is the spirit of the holy gods, and the king made him master of the magicians and astrologers.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the enchanters matter because they are the best Babylon has, and the best is not enough: no magician can tell the king his dream, and the man who can is the captive who prays. And I hold that the queen's memory is the verdict, that the Spirit of God in Daniel is greater than all the wisdom of Babylon.
